new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (+ text and page crops). (1) Quote at locator: printed p.141 (p.19), Appendix 'A comparative wordlist of the languages of Eastern Seram', reads verbatim: 'So unless otherwise stated the data presented below come from the following sources: Seti: Seti village / Bobot: Werinama / Masiwang: Kota Baru / Geser: Selor / Watubela: Efa / Banda: Elat [set as a column list in the original]. With regard to the phonetic notation, stress is penultimate unless otherwise marked.' The second part of the quote is at printed p.138 note 28, verbatim: 'The stress on the final syllable suggests that a suffixed genitive marker -ni ~ -in has changed the expected final a to e, i.e. metmetanni > metme…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Collins' own field transcription of Banda (Elat), stress is penultimate by default; only deviating items are marked, and in the 200-item Banda list roughly 19 words carry marked final stress (e.g. erén 'path', omá 'come', moɲǰón 'dirty', rasté 'hunt', karát, lafár, munít, noitík, ndeték, feferúŋ, rarón, fofán, runík, ansá, ŋelekár, ǰiŋár, fafót, namár (Eli), ndatarák (Eli)); Collins explains at least one final-stressed form as the residue of a lost suffix. I.e. penultimate word stress with a lexical minority of final-stressed words.
new_statements.exceptions: Final stress marked on c. 19 of c. 200 Banda items in the appendix (both consonant- and vowel-final words); note 28 attributes final stress in metmetén 'black' to loss of a suffix -ni ~ -; One item shows variation fafot ~ fafót.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms in an elicited 200-word comparative list (single words, some with person-marker hyphens); the stress remark is a transcription convention covering all six East Seram languages in the appendix, not a prose description of Banda prosody specifically.
new_statements.identity_note: Collins' Banda data are from Elat village (Banda-Elat, Glottolog dialect elat1240) with a few items marked (E) from Eli (elii1237); both are the two surviving varieties of band1355 on Kei Besar. Beware: the 'Banda' lists in Stokhof 1982a (Holle lists 3/3, PL D-49) are Banda Malay of the Banda Islands, not this language.

new_statements.quote: It is not surprising that materials which derive from research conducted by two different authors two decades apart will display some inconsistencies which cannot be regularized without distorting the available data. For example, in Appendix I stress is marked when it is not penultimate. This procedure has not been followed in other appendices.

For example, in Appendix I stress is marked when it is not penultimate. This procedure has not been followed in other appendices.' The saved 150-dpi crop shows the…
new_statements.relation_note: Same convention and same author as the existing statement (Collins 1986 p.141 'stress is penultimate unless otherwise marked', Banda data from Elat): default penultimate with a lexical minority of final-stressed forms marked. Compatible with the catalog record (penult penultimate stress). Adds that the 1977 text is from Banda Eli (the 1986 wordlist was Elat), so the penult-default-with-marked-final-exceptions picture holds for both villages per Collins.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Penultimate stress is treated as the default for Bandanese: in Appendix I (a Banda Eli narrative recorded by Collins in 1977) only non-penultimate stress is marked, and the marked cases are a minority of words carrying an acute on the final syllable (e.g. monó? '2p+make+TR', rosombál '3p+sail', nirobiŋán '3p+GEN+plate', sambál '1p+sail', tanáŋ 'peaceful' on p. 560). The article has no dedicated phonology/stress section; the body treats verb inflection, syncope (pp. 529-532, with a remark that 'pragmatic, or even prosodic factors' may condition syncope) and sociolinguistics.
new_statements.exceptions: Non-penultimate (final) stress exists on some words and is marked with an acute in Appendix I only (examples above); no rule for these is given. Other appendices (II-IV, Kaartinen 1992-96) carry no stress marking.
new_statements.identity_note: Appendix I of Collins & Kaartinen 1998 is a text recorded in Banda Eli (1977); the earlier Collins 1986 wordlist was from Banda Elat. The article notes minor dialect differences between the two villages (1sg marking c- vs s-, cluster retention) but nothing about stress differing.
